description: Add an Abstraction Lock immediately after Scope Lock so Frame Conn repository work cannot drop below the established diagnostic/planning abstraction without an explicit higher-level grant.
planning_goal: Create and integrate a deterministic Abstraction Lock into the canonical toolchain runtime immediately after Scope Lock. The lock must require repository investigation to proceed through existing generated intelligence and planning surfaces, deny generic source exploration and guessed file access by default, permit lower-level source access only when an existing higher-level toolchain artifact explicitly grants the path, and preserve the existing Scope Lock, diagnostics, planning, FilePatcher, validation, and terminal-state authorities.

authorized_deliverables: Create an Abstraction Lock for the Frame Conn toolchain.
Integrate it immediately after Scope Lock in the canonical runtime flow.
Make lower-level repository/source access require an explicit grant from the established higher-level toolchain evidence.
Teach and verify the Abstraction Lock in onboarding so dropping below the abstraction is rejected rather than merely discouraged.
forbidden_expansions: Do not modify application, game, UI, system_bridge, runtime, or feature source code.
Do not modify GitHub workflows or repository infrastructure.
Do not build a ChatGPT/GitHub gateway plugin in this change.
Do not redesign Scope Lock, FilePatcher, diagnostics, Patch Corridor, Corridor Context, Patch Staging, Change Propagation, or validation beyond the minimum integration required for Abstraction Lock.
Do not perform unrelated toolchain cleanup or refactoring.
authorized_capabilities: Abstraction Lock enforcement inside the existing dev_scripts toolchain only

acceptance_criteria: A dedicated Abstraction Lock implementation exists under dev_scripts and has deterministic machine-readable ALLOW, ABSTRACTION_VIOLATION, and ABSTRACTION_GAP outcomes.
The canonical runtime evaluates Abstraction Lock immediately after Scope Lock and before Mutation Carrier Router/orchestration proceeds.

The default Frame Conn repository-investigation abstraction permits established generated intelligence and planning surfaces: Symbol Families, Dependency Watershed/Graph, Integration Surface Atlas, Runtime Signal Map, Effect Atlas, Native Contract Catalog, Patch Corridor, Corridor Context, Patch Staging, Change Propagation, FilePatcher, and canonical validation.
Generic GitHub/source search and guessed/ad-hoc file reads are denied for repository investigation unless a higher-level toolchain artifact has explicitly granted the requested source path.
A grant is bounded to explicit path(s), records its issuing higher-level artifact/evidence, and cannot broaden the immutable Scope Lock.
An evidence gap returns ABSTRACTION_GAP with only the specifically permitted escalation; it does not authorize arbitrary lower-level exploration.
Toolchain modification remains denied unless the Scope Lock explicitly authorizes toolchain modification, as this request does.

Onboarding exercises the abstraction boundary: direct generic search is rejected, guessed source access is rejected, mapped/granted source access is accepted, and unrelated source access remains rejected.
Existing Scope Lock authority remains unchanged: Abstraction Lock constrains interfaces/levels and may not redefine or broaden the user objective.
Existing Patch Corridor, Corridor Context, Patch Staging, Change Propagation, FilePatcher, diagnostics, validation, and terminal-state behavior remain authoritative and otherwise unchanged.
Canonical validation and onboarding pass after the change.
non_goals: Build or replace the GitHub plugin.
Create a second diagnostic or planning system.
Permit the assistant to self-authorize abstraction descent.
